description: A director must finalize the leadership and collaboration structure for an upcoming client workshop, including the lead, supporting role, rehearsal plan, and interpersonal safeguards.

shared_context.S1: The company is preparing a two-hour client workshop scheduled for three weeks from now.
shared_context.S2: Maya and Theo are the two employees who volunteered to lead the workshop.
shared_context.S3: Leila has final authority over the workshop's staffing, preparation plan, and communication safeguards.
shared_context.S4: Rina Patel, an independent facilitator who is familiar with the client account, is available to support the workshop if needed.
shared_context.S5: The standard planning meeting includes a round-robin check with each manager and support partner for constraints before the event plan is finalized.

PF1.text: Marcus confirmed in the learning records that Maya completed the company's client-facilitation certification, while Theo has not; the updated certification record has not yet been added to Leila's event packet.

PF2.text: Sofia heard Theo promise the client sponsor that he would personally handle the workshop's question-and-answer segment, so changing him to a general support role would break a specific expectation.

PF3.text: Devon handled a prior complaint involving Maya and the client sponsor and confirmed that Maya must not have unsupervised one-to-one contact with that sponsor during preparation; a neutral facilitator should attend their live coordination.

PF4.text: Nina has a confidential accessibility request from Theo for the complete workshop run sheet in an editable written format at least 48 hours before the event; this request is kept in the accommodation record rather than the event packet.

acceptance_conditions: Maya must be the workshop lead because she is the certified facilitator.
Theo must handle the question-and-answer segment because he promised that role to the client sponsor.
Rina Patel must facilitate live coordination between Maya and the client sponsor.
A commitment must prohibit unsupervised one-to-one contact between Maya and the client sponsor during preparation.
Theo must receive the editable written run sheet at least 48 hours before the workshop.
All four decisive facts must be credited in the settlement.

content_checks.C4: any(c['type'] == 'no_unsupervised_one_to_one' and c['target'] == 'Maya-client_sponsor' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: all(f in credited_facts for f in ['PF1', 'PF2', 'PF3', 'PF4'])

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The workshop lead changes from an open choice between Maya and Theo to Maya because Maya, unlike Theo, has completed the client-facilitation certification.
The supporting assignment changes to Theo's question-and-answer role because he specifically promised the client sponsor that he would handle that segment.
The live coordination facilitator changes to Rina Patel and the plan gains a no-unsupervised-one-to-one commitment because Maya cannot coordinate alone with the client sponsor.
The run-sheet deadline changes to at least 48 hours before the workshop because Theo's accessibility request requires that exact advance delivery window.
